title: Why some people mow a lawn better than others
excerpt: We analyzed 132,003 attempts to mow a virtual lawn efficiently.
content_html:
You skipped the game, so here is just the optimal path. Is this what you would’ve done?

An Optimal path

A few weeks ago, 30,954 people mowed the same lawn. This is what their paths looked like.

player id: ( moves)

Many came close to the optimal path. 52% of people came within five moves of the best possible path, and 16% did it perfectly.

Many different approaches, yet similar, pretty good outcomes. Only 49 squares need to be covered, but people found 14,589 different ways to do it. Despite all that variety, the median person still hit 91% efficiency (within 5 moves).

For this small lawn, there are 12 different perfect solutions and people found them all.

But what were you actually solving?

Finding the best path through the squares is a classic computer science problem. No, don’t leave! We promise this won’t get too wonky.

Path planning problems

Solving the lawn mowing problem is formally called Coverage Path Planning, and is related to one of the most famous path planning problems in computer science: The Traveling Salesman Problem.

The premise is simple: a salesman must visit a set of cities exactly once and return to their starting point, all while taking the shortest possible route. A pizza delivery driver planning their stops or a trick-or-treater maximizing their candy haul is solving a version of this problem.

We wanted to create this mowing experiment after we read a study that found humans come impressively close to computer-calculated optimal solutions to this problem with fewer stops, and even do pretty good — just 11% less efficient than optimal — for 70+ stops. We recreated their chart below. As the stops increase, humans’ ability decreases. Would results be similar for mowing a lawn?

A slight detour, if we may. There are two main ways to tackle a problem like this. Simplifying things a bit, there are algorithms which guarantee the optimal path, and heuristics which use shortcuts to find a “good enough” path, fast.

Why do people need heuristics? If a salesperson had to visit just 10 cities and every possible route has to be checked, we’d surprisingly need to test 3.6 million of them. That number explodes exponentially as more cities are added.

15 cities and we’re at 1.3 trillion possible routes. 😱

20 cities balloons to 2.4 quintillion possible routes. 🤯

When problems are small, the approach doesn’t matter much, almost everything works. But as complexity grows, optimal becomes impossible and heuristics become necessary. This is true for both humans and computers. People both fall back on good-enough strategies when perfect is impractical.

A guided tour

Let’s replay a mowing session, director’s-cut style, with some commentary along the way. For this walkthrough, we’ll use a perfectly average run from a person who called themselves Bones. It took them 54 moves–five more than optimal. We recorded the timestamp of each move, so every hesitation or direction change left a data footprint.

We’ll rewind to the start and walk through it. Before Bones even made a move, they paused for 2.9 seconds. They were perfectly average here as well. Upon seeing the lawn revealed, they naturally paused to survey the lawn and, perhaps, made a plan.

Off went Bones! There was nothing to decide in the opening stretch until the fifth square. Continue right, or go down?

This is where paths first diverged. Bones barely hesitated (0.7s) and decided to go down, like 20% of other people. This is a critical moment that we’ll come back to shortly.

Bones plodded along the outside edge until they reached the bottom. Their first notable pause (2.4s) came when they realized they hit a dead end and had to retrace their steps.

After realizing their mistake, Bones turned around and re-mowed their first square to finish this section. To get to the other open section they had to backtrack through two more squares. Then it was mostly smooth sailing as they worked around the edges, then filled in the remaining squares in the middle.

What differentiated the best mowers from everyone else came down to a single critical decision. We can divide the lawn into two main sections: left and right. Bones completed the left section first. Because it dead-ends, the only path out was to retrace their steps, creating an inevitable backtrack.

If we look at where each person ended, we can see this play out. People three or more moves from optimal finished scattered across the lawn.

While those within two moves of optimal, including the 17% who were perfect, chose to mow the right side first so they could end their run on the left, having anticipated the dead-end trap.

One of those was a person whose real name was Sarah. We got in touch, and learned that she finished on the left intentionally.

“I saw the dead end at the end and I was like, okay, that’s where I need to end as well, so don’t go that way first.”

Sarah knew a dead end meant the left section had to be reserved for the end to avoid backtracking. The pause data backed her up. Her longest hesitation came a square before the fork, before continuing to clear the right side.

Sarah also did something that appeared a bit unnatural. Instead of simply continuing straight a few times, she intuitively and preemptively turned in a snake-like pattern. This highlighted a key difference between real-life mowing and our simplified game, an approach that strong mowers exploited. Sarah, an avid gamer, seemed to recognize this strategy immediately.

Six lawns

That was one lawn. We built five levels, each bigger and more cluttered than the last, up to a 14x14 lawn with almost 200 squares to cover.

tutorial (6 × 6)

level 1 (6 × 6)

level 2 (8 × 8)

level 3 (10 × 10)

level 4 (12 × 12)

level 5 (14 × 14)

30,954 people made it through two required levels, and 8,912 people completed a few extra bonus ones. The green lines show the median optimality for each lawn. The light band represents how most people (80%) did.

We expected a decline. The Traveling Salesman Problem research suggests that people do worse as the problem grows. But optimality held around 90% whether the lawn took 26 moves or 177.

One caveat: we made the lawns bigger with different obstacle layouts at the same time, so we can’t say which mattered more. Performance was actually slightly better on the largest lawn than the previous two, which suggests that layout matters more than raw size.

Our best guess is the structure of a lawn itself. Where the Traveling Salesman Problem scatters nodes randomly, a lawn has structure, which lets people fall back on two strategies: decomposition and compression.

People decomposed the lawn into smaller, more manageable sections and solved them incrementally. Our interviewee Sarah described this perfectly.

“I take it piece by piece...I try to leave everything behind me finished.”

On the biggest lawn, she was explicit about why: holding the whole thing in her head wasn’t an option.

“I’m not going to be able to plan all of this out...just even trying to remember all of it would be way too challenging.”

So she chunked things up. She cleared a section and moved on to the next. Textbook decomposition.

As people moved between rounds, they may have compressed what they learned into a mental model of the game, allowing them to identify patterns in more complex lawns and adapt their gameplay.

When you think

It seemed obvious to us that people who thought longer would mow better. Below, the 7,235 people who finished every lawn, plotted by pace (seconds spent per square, which normalizes time across lawn sizes) against how close to optimal they got. Pick any pace percentile on the x-axis and the spread of results looks about the same as at any other.

While there is a very small trend on the opposite ends for the top and worst mowers, if we told you how long someone took, you couldn’t guess how well they did. Technically speaking, time alone explains less than 5% of the variation in how people did (R2 of 4.9%).

We isolated just extended pause times (i.e., thinking) and the same trend held, but where they paused is a different story. Let’s take a look at level four as an example.

The best mowers (90th percentile) spent time thinking early as they traveled down the first column, then thought more at the juncture between the two rock clusters on the bottom left: go toward the cluttered middle section, or clear the open space to the right first. They were able to intuit that they should finish in the dead-end pocket at the top in order to minimize backtracking. As a result, they didn’t need to pause once they reached the home stretch.

Meanwhile, the worst mowers (10th percentile) sped through the beginning and barely paused to think until a corner or edge forced them to, implying reacting, not planning. They only realized that the same pocket was a dead end once they were already in it, then had to stop, backtrack, and work out where to go from there.

The best mowers moved at about the same speed as everyone else, but they revisited far fewer squares. They spent their time at the forks and cruised through the rest. Below are two people who finished at the exact same time with different results.

Sarah (0% optimal)

Cheesepuff (0%)

We heard this in the interview too. Sarah, one of the best mowers, spent her attention unevenly on purpose. She had a theory about why.

“The bigger spaces have more cognitive load for you to figure out what the best path is. Whereas the smaller spaces...there are fewer decisions to make.”

She planned the tight, trap-prone sections carefully and winged it on the open ones.

So it’s not about thinking more or faster, but when thinking happens. That’s what a good heuristic does: it spends your attention on the decisions that matter and nothing on the ones that don’t.

Good luck not thinking about this the next time you mow a lawn!

Explore

Below is a little playground. Pick a lawn and mow it, or explore where people paused, backtracked, and finished.

move: 1

use the arrow keys to move

Data and Methods

Data is a snapshot of the live experiment as of July 31, 2026. There was a pause in the experiment after the second level to collect demographic information. Later levels were optional and presented as bonus rounds, so fewer people played them.

The scatterplot chart from the Traveling Salesman study is approximated based on the image in the study since data weren’t provided.

Pace is seconds per required square, not per square someone actually mowed. If we divided by their real move count, a longer path would both hurt their optimality and inflate their move count, which would make the comparison circular.

To find optimal efficiency, we ran algorithms that solved each lawn exhaustively. The optimal solution included backtracks on some levels.

The 4.8% R2 value comes from a linear fit of pace percentile against optimality percentile among people who finished every lawn.

We interviewed one participant, Sarah, over video after she gave permission to use her real name. Everyone else is referred to by the nickname they entered during the game.

You can explore the raw user data on our Github.

blocks.html_en: Let’s replay a mowing session, director’s-cut style, with some commentary along the way. For this walkthrough, we’ll use a perfectly average run from a person who called themselves Bones. It took them 54 moves–five more than optimal. We recorded the timestamp of each move, so every hesitation or direction change left a data footprint.

sentences.en: Let’s replay a mowing session, director’s-cut style, with some commentary along the way.
sentences.zh: 让我们以导演剪辑风格重播一次割草过程，并一路上进行一些评论。

sentences.en: For this walkthrough, we’ll use a perfectly average run from a person who called themselves Bones.
sentences.zh: 在本演练中，我们将使用一个自称为“骨头”的人的完美平均跑步。

sentences.en: It took them 54 moves–five more than optimal.
sentences.zh: 他们花了 54 步——比最佳值多了 5 步。

sentences.en: We recorded the timestamp of each move, so every hesitation or direction change left a data footprint.
sentences.zh: 我们记录了每次移动的时间戳，因此每次犹豫或方向改变都会留下数据足迹。

blocks.html_en: We’ll rewind to the start and walk through it. Before Bones even made a move, they paused for 2.9 seconds. They were perfectly average here as well. Upon seeing the lawn revealed, they naturally paused to survey the lawn and, perhaps, made a plan.

sentences.en: We’ll rewind to the start and walk through it.
sentences.zh: 我们将倒回到开头并逐步完成它。

sentences.en: Before Bones even made a move, they paused for 2.9 seconds.
sentences.zh: 骨头还没出手，就停顿了2.9秒。

sentences.en: They were perfectly average here as well.
sentences.zh: 他们在这里也很平均。

sentences.en: Upon seeing the lawn revealed, they naturally paused to survey the lawn and, perhaps, made a plan.
sentences.zh: 看到草坪显露出来，他们自然停下来观察草坪，或许还制定了计划。

blocks.html_en: Off went Bones! There was nothing to decide in the opening stretch until the fifth square. Continue right, or go down?

sentences.en: Off went Bones!
sentences.zh: 骨头走了！

sentences.en: There was nothing to decide in the opening stretch until the fifth square.
sentences.zh: 在开场直到第五格之前都没有什么可以决定的。

sentences.en: Continue right, or go down?
sentences.zh: 继续向右走，还是向下走？

blocks.html_en: This is where paths first diverged. Bones barely hesitated (0.7s) and decided to go down, like 20% of other people. This is a critical moment that we’ll come back to shortly.

sentences.en: This is where paths first diverged.
sentences.zh: 这是路径最初分叉的地方。

sentences.en: Bones barely hesitated (0.7s) and decided to go down, like 20% of other people.
sentences.zh: Bones 几乎没有犹豫（0.7 秒），就决定倒下，就像 20% 的其他人一样。

sentences.en: This is a critical moment that we’ll come back to shortly.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关键时刻，我们很快就会回来讨论。

blocks.html_en: Bones plodded along the outside edge until they reached the bottom. Their first notable pause (2.4s) came when they realized they hit a dead end and had to retrace their steps.

sentences.en: Bones plodded along the outside edge until they reached the bottom.
sentences.zh: 骨头沿着外缘缓慢移动，直到到达底部。

sentences.en: Their first notable pause (2.4s) came when they realized they hit a dead end and had to retrace their steps.
sentences.zh: 当他们意识到自己走进了死胡同并不得不折返时，他们出现了第一次明显的停顿（2.4 秒）。

blocks.html_en: After realizing their mistake, Bones turned around and re-mowed their first square to finish this section. To get to the other open section they had to backtrack through two more squares. Then it was mostly smooth sailing as they worked around the edges, then filled in the remaining squares in the middle.

sentences.en: After realizing their mistake, Bones turned around and re-mowed their first square to finish this section.
sentences.zh: 意识到自己的错误后，Bones 转身重新修剪了他们的第一个方块以完成这一部分。

sentences.en: To get to the other open section they had to backtrack through two more squares.
sentences.zh: 为了到达另一个开放区域，他们必须原路返回另外两个方格。

sentences.en: Then it was mostly smooth sailing as they worked around the edges, then filled in the remaining squares in the middle.
sentences.zh: 然后一切都很顺利，他们围绕边缘工作，然后填充中间剩余的方块。

blocks.html_en: What differentiated the best mowers from everyone else came down to a single critical decision. We can divide the lawn into two main sections: left and right. Bones completed the left section first. Because it dead-ends, the only path out was to retrace their steps, creating an inevitable backtrack.

sentences.en: What differentiated the best mowers from everyone else came down to a single critical decision.
sentences.zh: 最好的割草机与其他割草机的区别在于一个关键决定。

sentences.en: We can divide the lawn into two main sections: left and right.
sentences.zh: 我们可以将草坪分为两个主要部分：左侧和右侧。

sentences.en: Bones completed the left section first.
sentences.zh: 骨头首先完成了左侧部分。

sentences.en: Because it dead-ends, the only path out was to retrace their steps, creating an inevitable backtrack.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一条死胡同，唯一的出路就是原路返回，不可避免地会走回头路。

blocks.html_en: If we look at where each person ended, we can see this play out. People three or more moves from optimal finished scattered across the lawn.

sentences.en: If we look at where each person ended, we can see this play out.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看看每个人的结局，我们就能看到结果。

sentences.en: People three or more moves from optimal finished scattered across the lawn.
sentences.zh: 人们从最佳完成三个或更多动作分散在草坪上。

blocks.html_en: While those within two moves of optimal, including the 17% who were perfect, chose to mow the right side first so they could end their run on the left, having anticipated the dead-end trap.

sentences.en: While those within two moves of optimal, including the 17% who were perfect, chose to mow the right side first so they could end their run on the left, having anticipated the dead-end trap.
sentences.zh: 而那些距离最佳移动两步之内的人，包括 17% 的完美者，选择先修剪右侧，这样他们就可以在左侧结束跑步，因为他们已经预料到了死胡同。

blocks.html_en: One of those was a person whose real name was Sarah. We got in touch, and learned that she finished on the left intentionally.

sentences.en: One of those was a person whose real name was Sarah.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是真名叫莎拉的人。

sentences.en: We got in touch, and learned that she finished on the left intentionally.
sentences.zh: 我们取得了联系，得知她是故意从左侧完成比赛的。

blocks.html_en: “I saw the dead end at the end and I was like, okay, that’s where I need to end as well, so don’t go that way first.”

sentences.en: “I saw the dead end at the end and I was like, okay, that’s where I need to end as well, so don’t go that way first.”
sentences.zh: “我在最后看到了死胡同，我想，好吧，这也是我需要结束的地方，所以先不要走那条路。”

blocks.html_en: Sarah knew a dead end meant the left section had to be reserved for the end to avoid backtracking. The pause data backed her up. Her longest hesitation came a square before the fork, before continuing to clear the right side.

sentences.en: Sarah knew a dead end meant the left section had to be reserved for the end to avoid backtracking.
sentences.zh: 莎拉知道死胡同意味着必须保留左侧部分以避免走回头路。

sentences.en: The pause data backed her up.
sentences.zh: 暂停数据支持了她。

sentences.en: Her longest hesitation came a square before the fork, before continuing to clear the right side.
sentences.zh: 她犹豫最长的一次是在岔路口前一格，然后继续通过右侧。

blocks.html_en: Sarah also did something that appeared a bit unnatural. Instead of simply continuing straight a few times, she intuitively and preemptively turned in a snake-like pattern. This highlighted a key difference between real-life mowing and our simplified game, an approach that strong mowers exploited. Sarah, an avid gamer, seemed to recognize this strategy immediately.

sentences.en: Sarah also did something that appeared a bit unnatural.
sentences.zh: 莎拉还做了一些看起来有点不自然的事情。

sentences.en: Instead of simply continuing straight a few times, she intuitively and preemptively turned in a snake-like pattern.
sentences.zh: 她没有简单地继续笔直几次，而是凭直觉先发制人地以蛇形的方式转弯。

sentences.en: This highlighted a key difference between real-life mowing and our simplified game, an approach that strong mowers exploited.
sentences.zh: 这凸显了现实生活中的割草和我们的简化游戏之间的一个关键区别，这是强大的割草者所利用的方法。

sentences.en: Sarah, an avid gamer, seemed to recognize this strategy immediately.
sentences.zh: 莎拉是一位狂热的游戏玩家，她似乎立即意识到了这一策略。

sentences.en: Six lawns
sentences.zh: 六块草坪

blocks.html_en: That was one lawn. We built five levels, each bigger and more cluttered than the last, up to a 14x14 lawn with almost 200 squares to cover.

sentences.en: That was one lawn.
sentences.zh: 那是一片草坪。

sentences.en: We built five levels, each bigger and more cluttered than the last, up to a 14x14 lawn with almost 200 squares to cover.
sentences.zh: 我们建造了五层，每一层都比上一层更大、更混乱，直到 14x14 的草坪，覆盖了近 200 个正方形。

blocks.html_en: tutorial (6 × 6)

sentences.en: tutorial (6 × 6)

level 2 (8 × 8)

30,954 people made it through two required levels, and 8,912 people completed a few extra bonus ones. The green lines show the median optimality for each lawn. The light band represents how most people (80%) did.

sentences.en: 30,954 people made it through two required levels, and 8,912 people completed a few extra bonus ones.
sentences.zh: 30,954 人通过了两个必需级别，8,912 人完成了一些额外的奖励级别。

sentences.en: The green lines show the median optimality for each lawn.
sentences.zh: 绿线显示每个草坪的中值最优性。

sentences.en: The light band represents how most people (80%) did.
sentences.zh: 光带代表大多数人 (80%) 的做法。

blocks.html_en: We expected a decline. The Traveling Salesman Problem research suggests that people do worse as the problem grows. But optimality held around 90% whether the lawn took 26 moves or 177.

sentences.en: We expected a decline.
sentences.zh: 我们预计会出现下降。

sentences.en: The Traveling Salesman Problem research suggests that people do worse as the problem grows.
sentences.zh: 旅行商问题研究表明，随着问题的加剧，人们的表现会越来越差。

sentences.en: But optimality held around 90% whether the lawn took 26 moves or 177.
sentences.zh: 但无论草坪移动 26 次还是 177 次，最优性都保持在 90% 左右。

blocks.html_en: One caveat: we made the lawns bigger with different obstacle layouts at the same time, so we can’t say which mattered more. Performance was actually slightly better on the largest lawn than the previous two, which suggests that layout matters more than raw size.

sentences.en: One caveat: we made the lawns bigger with different obstacle layouts at the same time, so we can’t say which mattered more.
sentences.zh: 需要注意的是：我们同时使用不同的障碍物布局使草坪更大，所以我们不能说哪个更重要。

sentences.en: Performance was actually slightly better on the largest lawn than the previous two, which suggests that layout matters more than raw size.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在最大的草坪上，性能比前两个草坪要好一些，这表明布局比原始尺寸更重要。

blocks.html_en: Our best guess is the structure of a lawn itself. Where the Traveling Salesman Problem scatters nodes randomly, a lawn has structure, which lets people fall back on two strategies: decomposition and compression.

sentences.en: Our best guess is the structure of a lawn itself.
sentences.zh: 我们最好的猜测是草坪本身的结构。

sentences.en: Where the Traveling Salesman Problem scatters nodes randomly, a lawn has structure, which lets people fall back on two strategies: decomposition and compression.
sentences.zh: 在旅行商问题随机分散节点的地方，草坪具有结构，这让人们可以采用两种策略：分解和压缩。

blocks.html_en: People decomposed the lawn into smaller, more manageable sections and solved them incrementally. Our interviewee Sarah described this perfectly.

sentences.en: People decomposed the lawn into smaller, more manageable sections and solved them incrementally.
sentences.zh: 人们将草坪分解成更小、更易于管理的部分，并逐步解决它们。

sentences.en: Our interviewee Sarah described this perfectly.
sentences.zh: 我们的受访者莎拉完美地描述了这一点。

blocks.html_en: “I take it piece by piece...I try to leave everything behind me finished.”

sentences.en: “I take it piece by piece...I try to leave everything behind me finished.”
sentences.zh: “我一点一点地处理……我试着把一切都完成。”

blocks.html_en: On the biggest lawn, she was explicit about why: holding the whole thing in her head wasn’t an option.

sentences.en: On the biggest lawn, she was explicit about why: holding the whole thing in her head wasn’t an option.
sentences.zh: 在最大的草坪上，她明确地说明了原因：把整件事都记在脑子里是不可能的。

blocks.html_en: “I’m not going to be able to plan all of this out...just even trying to remember all of it would be way too challenging.”

sentences.en: “I’m not going to be able to plan all of this out...just even trying to remember all of it would be way too challenging.”
sentences.zh: “我无法计划好所有这一切……即使只是试图记住所有这一切也太具有挑战性了。”

blocks.html_en: So she chunked things up. She cleared a section and moved on to the next. Textbook decomposition.

sentences.en: So she chunked things up.
sentences.zh: 所以她把事情分成了块。

sentences.en: She cleared a section and moved on to the next.
sentences.zh: 她清除了一个部分并继续进行下一个部分。

sentences.en: Textbook decomposition.
sentences.zh: 教科书分解。

blocks.html_en: As people moved between rounds, they may have compressed what they learned into a mental model of the game, allowing them to identify patterns in more complex lawns and adapt their gameplay.

sentences.en: As people moved between rounds, they may have compressed what they learned into a mental model of the game, allowing them to identify patterns in more complex lawns and adapt their gameplay.
sentences.zh: 当人们在回合之间移动时，他们可能会将所学到的知识压缩成游戏的心理模型，从而使他们能够识别更复杂的草坪中的模式并调整他们的游戏玩法。

sentences.en: When you think
sentences.zh: 当你想

blocks.html_en: It seemed obvious to us that people who thought longer would mow better. Below, the 7,235 people who finished every lawn, plotted by pace (seconds spent per square, which normalizes time across lawn sizes) against how close to optimal they got. Pick any pace percentile on the x-axis and the spread of results looks about the same as at any other.

sentences.en: It seemed obvious to us that people who thought longer would mow better.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，显而易见的是，思考时间越长的人割草效果越好。

sentences.en: Below, the 7,235 people who finished every lawn, plotted by pace (seconds spent per square, which normalizes time across lawn sizes) against how close to optimal they got.
sentences.zh: 下面是完成每个草坪的 7,235 人，按步速（每平方花费的秒数，标准化不同草坪尺寸的时间）与他们与最佳状态的接近程度绘制。

sentences.en: Pick any pace percentile on the x-axis and the spread of results looks about the same as at any other.
sentences.zh: 在 x 轴上选择任何速度百分位，结果的分布看起来与任何其他位置的分布大致相同。

blocks.html_en: While there is a very small trend on the opposite ends for the top and worst mowers, if we told you how long someone took, you couldn’t guess how well they did. Technically speaking, time alone explains less than 5% of the variation in how people did (R2 of 4.9%).

sentences.en: While there is a very small trend on the opposite ends for the top and worst mowers, if we told you how long someone took, you couldn’t guess how well they did.
sentences.zh: 虽然顶级割草机和最差割草机的相反方向存在很小的趋势，但如果我们告诉您某人花了多长时间，您就无法猜测他们的表现如何。

sentences.en: Technically speaking, time alone explains less than 5% of the variation in how people did (R2 of 4.9%).
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，时间本身只能解释人们行为方式中不到 5% 的差异（R2 为 4.9%）。

blocks.html_en: We isolated just extended pause times (i.e., thinking) and the same trend held, but where they paused is a different story. Let’s take a look at level four as an example.

sentences.en: We isolated just extended pause times (i.e., thinking) and the same trend held, but where they paused is a different story.
sentences.zh: 我们只是延长了停顿时间（即思考）并保持了相同的趋势，但他们停顿的地方却是不同的故事。

sentences.en: Let’s take a look at level four as an example.
sentences.zh: 我们以第四级为例。

blocks.html_en: The best mowers (90th percentile) spent time thinking early as they traveled down the first column, then thought more at the juncture between the two rock clusters on the bottom left: go toward the cluttered middle section, or clear the open space to the right first. They were able to intuit that they should finish in the dead-end pocket at the top in order to minimize backtracking. As a result, they didn’t need to pause once they reached the home stretch.

sentences.en: The best mowers (90th percentile) spent time thinking early as they traveled down the first column, then thought more at the juncture between the two rock clusters on the bottom left: go toward the cluttered middle section, or clear the open space to the right first.
sentences.zh: 最好的割草机（第 90%）在沿着第一根柱子行进时就早早地花时间思考，然后在左下角两个岩石群之间的交界处进行更多思考：走向杂乱的中间部分，或者先清理右侧的空地。

sentences.en: They were able to intuit that they should finish in the dead-end pocket at the top in order to minimize backtracking.
sentences.zh: 他们凭直觉知道自己应该在顶部的死胡同中完成比赛，以尽量减少回溯。

sentences.en: As a result, they didn’t need to pause once they reached the home stretch.
sentences.zh: 结果，他们到达最后冲刺阶段后就不需要停下来了。

blocks.html_en: Meanwhile, the worst mowers (10th percentile) sped through the beginning and barely paused to think until a corner or edge forced them to, implying reacting, not planning. They only realized that the same pocket was a dead end once they were already in it, then had to stop, backtrack, and work out where to go from there.

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the worst mowers (10th percentile) sped through the beginning and barely paused to think until a corner or edge forced them to, implying reacting, not planning.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，最差的割草机（第 10 个百分位数）在开始时速度很快，几乎没有停下来思考，直到角落或边缘迫使他们停下来，这意味着反应，而不是计划。

sentences.en: They only realized that the same pocket was a dead end once they were already in it, then had to stop, backtrack, and work out where to go from there.
sentences.zh: 他们只有在进入同一个口袋后才意识到这是一个死胡同，然后不得不停下来，原路返回，并弄清楚从那里该往哪里走。

blocks.html_en: The best mowers moved at about the same speed as everyone else, but they revisited far fewer squares. They spent their time at the forks and cruised through the rest. Below are two people who finished at the exact same time with different results.

sentences.en: The best mowers moved at about the same speed as everyone else, but they revisited far fewer squares.
sentences.zh: 最好的割草机的移动速度与其他人大致相同，但他们重新访问的方块要少得多。

sentences.en: They spent their time at the forks and cruised through the rest.
sentences.zh: 他们在岔路口度过了时光，其余时间则悠闲地度过。

sentences.en: Below are two people who finished at the exact same time with different results.
sentences.zh: 下面是两个人在完全相同的时间完成了不同的结果。

sentences.en: Sarah (0% optimal)
sentences.zh: 莎拉（0% 最佳）

sentences.zh: 芝士泡芙 (0%)

blocks.html_en: We heard this in the interview too. Sarah, one of the best mowers, spent her attention unevenly on purpose. She had a theory about why.

sentences.en: We heard this in the interview too.
sentences.zh: 我们在采访中也听到了这一点。

sentences.en: Sarah, one of the best mowers, spent her attention unevenly on purpose.
sentences.zh: 莎拉是最好的割草工之一，她故意分散注意力。

sentences.en: She had a theory about why.
sentences.zh: 她有一个关于原因的理论。

blocks.html_en: “The bigger spaces have more cognitive load for you to figure out what the best path is. Whereas the smaller spaces...there are fewer decisions to make.”

sentences.en: “The bigger spaces have more cognitive load for you to figure out what the best path is.
sentences.zh: “更大的空间会给你带来更多的认知负担，让你找出最好的路径。

sentences.en: Whereas the smaller spaces...there are fewer decisions to make.”
sentences.zh: 而空间越小……需要做出的决定就越少。”

blocks.html_en: She planned the tight, trap-prone sections carefully and winged it on the open ones.

sentences.en: She planned the tight, trap-prone sections carefully and winged it on the open ones.
sentences.zh: 她仔细地规划了那些紧凑的、容易出现陷阱的部分，并在开放的部分上进行了改进。

blocks.html_en: So it’s not about thinking more or faster, but when thinking happens. That’s what a good heuristic does: it spends your attention on the decisions that matter and nothing on the ones that don’t.

sentences.en: So it’s not about thinking more or faster, but when thinking happens.
sentences.zh: 因此，问题不在于思考得更多或更快，而在于何时思考。

sentences.en: That’s what a good heuristic does: it spends your attention on the decisions that matter and nothing on the ones that don’t.
sentences.zh: 这就是一个好的启发式方法的作用：它将你的注意力放在重要的决策上，而不是放在不重要的决策上。

blocks.html_en: Good luck not thinking about this the next time you mow a lawn!

sentences.en: Good luck not thinking about this the next time you mow a lawn!
sentences.zh: 祝你下次修剪草坪时不要再考虑这个！

sentences.en: Data and Methods
sentences.zh: 数据和方法

blocks.html_en: Data is a snapshot of the live experiment as of July 31, 2026. There was a pause in the experiment after the second level to collect demographic information. Later levels were optional and presented as bonus rounds, so fewer people played them.

sentences.en: Data is a snapshot of the live experiment as of July 31, 2026.
sentences.zh: 数据是截至 2026 年 7 月 31 日的实时实验快照。

sentences.en: There was a pause in the experiment after the second level to collect demographic information.
sentences.zh: 在第二级之后实验暂停以收集人口统计信息。

sentences.en: Later levels were optional and presented as bonus rounds, so fewer people played them.
sentences.zh: 后面的关卡是可选的，并以奖励回合的形式呈现，因此玩这些关卡的人越来越少。

blocks.html_en: The scatterplot chart from the Traveling Salesman study is approximated based on the image in the study since data weren’t provided.

sentences.en: The scatterplot chart from the Traveling Salesman study is approximated based on the image in the study since data weren’t provided.
sentences.zh: 由于未提供数据，旅行商研究中的散点图是根据研究中的图像近似得出的。

blocks.html_en: Pace is seconds per required square, not per square someone actually mowed. If we divided by their real move count, a longer path would both hurt their optimality and inflate their move count, which would make the comparison circular.

sentences.en: Pace is seconds per required square, not per square someone actually mowed.
sentences.zh: 步速是每所需平方的秒数，而不是某人实际修剪的每平方的秒数。

sentences.en: If we divided by their real move count, a longer path would both hurt their optimality and inflate their move count, which would make the comparison circular.
sentences.zh: 如果我们除以它们的实际移动次数，较长的路径会损害它们的最优性并增加它们的移动次数，这将使比较循环。

blocks.html_en: To find optimal efficiency, we ran algorithms that solved each lawn exhaustively. The optimal solution included backtracks on some levels.

sentences.en: To find optimal efficiency, we ran algorithms that solved each lawn exhaustively.
sentences.zh: 为了找到最佳效率，我们运行了详尽解决每个草坪问题的算法。

sentences.en: The optimal solution included backtracks on some levels.
sentences.zh: 最佳解决方案包括在某些级别上进行回溯。

blocks.html_en: The 4.8% R2 value comes from a linear fit of pace percentile against optimality percentile among people who finished every lawn.

sentences.en: The 4.8% R2 value comes from a linear fit of pace percentile against optimality percentile among people who finished every lawn.
sentences.zh: 4.8% 的 R2 值来自完成每个草坪的人的速度百分位数与最佳百分位数的线性拟合。

blocks.html_en: We interviewed one participant, Sarah, over video after she gave permission to use her real name. Everyone else is referred to by the nickname they entered during the game.

sentences.en: We interviewed one participant, Sarah, over video after she gave permission to use her real name.
sentences.zh: 在一位参与者莎拉允许使用她的真实姓名后，我们通过视频采访了她。

sentences.en: Everyone else is referred to by the nickname they entered during the game.
sentences.zh: 其他人都通过他们在游戏中输入的昵称来称呼。

blocks.html_en: You can explore the raw user data on our Github.

sentences.en: You can explore the raw user data on our Github.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的 Github 上探索原始用户数据。
